questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1. I really wanted to go to an english speaking country to improve my english
2. I really loved the school (it is so beautiful) 
3. I liked that it is placed close to lots of cool places to go on hikes and trips and so on in Scotland (like the highlands) 
4. It is much cheaper than going to USA or Australia
5. Closer to home, so easier for visitors. I got 2 visits during my stay from friends and family, which was really nice!!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, though you do get information from a bunch of different places, so the diffucult thing was to remember where you find the specific information you need. I think the visiting students team at GU were great. There are also the My SRC app which contains a lot of information on the intro-events that begin even 2 weeks prior to teaching starting. Otherwise I would advise you to find relevent instagrams for the university, your faculty at the university and the international students at GU instagram (a lot of them are called something with UofG in the name, so seach that)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of information on orientation, welcome address, campus tours, Ceilidhs (which i would advise you to go to!!), and so on. Keep an eye on your email, the instagrams and ask around for information (people here are more than happy to help!!)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I would give it a 5/5, but the one minus is that the information is spread out on several different platforms, which could be a bit confusing.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I would send an application for student housing through the University as soon as possible. I think they give the rooms in order of who applies first. However, not everyone gets an offer from them (I didn't and ended up kind of desperate...). So I would also look at private student accommodation early on (in june maybe) and try to find something in the West End of Glasgow! That is the place to be!! Anything under 200 gbp. pr. week is a good deal, if you want ensuite.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is good and fine as long as you are close to the uni. I preferred a dorm, so I would meet other students where I live, as I was going all alone, but you can also find rooms/apartments on Spareroom and services like that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not satisfied with the housing available by the Uni, but if you are out in good time, you should be able to find some nice accommodation close to Uni.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy - Keep an eye on your mail and follow the instructions.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A little bit hectic, as you only get to choose your courses in the few weeks before classes start. But I mostly found it hectic because I had to get the courses I had gotten pre-approved by KU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a visiting students team, who answers all questions. However, they were only three, so sometimes it would take a few days to get a reply. I also reached out to the lecturers of the courses I wanted when the visiting students team couldn't help me register for them, and they were very helpful!!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I reached out to the lecturers of the courses I wanted when the visiting students team couldn't help me register for them, and they were very helpful!!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit more like how high school is in Denmark with smaller class sizes and much contact with the lecturers, which was very fun to try. The academic level is a bit lower than in Denmark, in my opinion.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Two out of my three classes were honours-level classes, which just means, that they are not for first-year students. The level was not too difficult at all

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As I said, it is a bit more like high school with more verbal participation, and they also check attendance. However, they don't really use the attendance for anything (I don't think at least)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POLITIC4149 Authoritarianism: Concepts, Theories and Comparative Analysis 
POLITIC4020 Politics Of The European Union
ADED2052E Nationalism, Democracy and  Self-Determination since the French Revolution

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the authoritarianism class. But all the courses I took was to get DAK and EP approved, so I wish I had been able to take some courses of my own choosing as well

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I bought a bike for about 200 gbp, which I sold back to the bike-shop after my stay for 100 gbp.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out and eating at restaurants was a bit cheaper than in Copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: GU has soooo many clubs you can join. They have days at the beginning of the semester, where all the clubs have little stalls around campus where you can hear about each of them and see wether you want to join. I went to multiple events (sports, dance, arts and crafts, hikes and so on) but did not join any club.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many activities available. All the clubs host an assortment of events and activities, which you can find on an app called SRC-app

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining one of the clubs or one of the sports teams!! Also the arts and crafts night each week is such a fun activity to do with your friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I went on multiple trips during my stay, and I can recommend all of them!
1. Going to Inverness to see the city and go on hikes (also went to see Loch Ness) 
2. Going to the Isle of Skye for a weekend. Sooo pretty!!
3. Going to Ireland for a weekend (both Dublin + a trip to Galway and the Cliffs of Moher) 
4. Going to London. Saw all the sights and went to see a musical in the West End, where there are a bunch of theatres 
5. Exploring Glasgow (the west and east ends) -> Barrowland, the cathedral + the necropolis, Tennents brewery, Kelvingrove Museum, and so on. 
6. Taking a one-day-trip to Edinburgh 

Being in Glasgow you are close to the beautiful nature in the highlands and also to citylife. 

If you (or some of you friends) are up for it, I would highly suggest that you rent a car and take a trip up to the highlands!! It is so amazing!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. The culture is not so different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not any tips in particular. Talking with the other students in your classes is a good place to start. I also went to a bunch of the intro-week-activities and met a bunch of people who are now my friends there!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I feel like people were very talkative and very good at asking how you are and so on. Some teachers also checked in on how I was adjusting to living in Scotland, as I was the only exchange student in two of my classes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy it and make the most out of your exchange! It flies by!! 
2. Start looking early (may/june) for places to live close to campus (preferably in the west end, in my opinion). 
3. Go on trips, but be sure to also explore Glasgow!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I would say the friends I made!! 
But also all the nature experiences with hikes in the beautiful nature in the scottish highlands

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me, it was my living situation. I lived kinda far from uni, towards the north/east end of the city. About 15 minutes on my bike from the uni. But it was honestly not a big challenge at all.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
